name: AlphaVerus
one_liner: A model translates programs into Verus, tree search repairs them with verifier feedback, and a filter keeps trustworthy results as examples.

loop.proposes: Verus translations of programs (from Dafny) and repaired versions, from a Llama 3.1 70B model
loop.judged_by: The Verus verifier, plus a filter that rejects translations whose specification or program is misaligned
loop.steers: Treefinement tree search fixes errors from verifier feedback; verified, filtered programs become prompt examples

headline_result: With Llama 3.1 70B and no model fine-tuning, verified-code generation reaches 32.9% on HumanEval-Verus and 65.7% on MBPP-verified (pass@256), versus 27.1% and 35.9% for GPT-4o and 11.8% and 26.9% for Llama 3.1 70B.
caveat: HumanEval-Verus and MBPP-verified are small, hand-adapted benchmarks, and the task is generating code plus proofs from specifications. Verification proves code matches the specification, so the misalignment filter matters.
beyond_harness_note: Verus judges validity, a tree of candidate repairs is searched, and a built-in filter guards against the model gaming the verifier.
algorithmic_authority: Verus verifier with a misalignment filter

sources.title: AlphaVerus: Bootstrapping Formally Verified Code Generation through Self-Improving Translation and Treefinement

verification.notes: Read abstract and Table 2 of the PDF text. Report said 'translation to verified code for HumanEval/MBPP-style tasks': the translation step builds exemplars from DafnyBench (Dafny to Verus); HumanEval and MBPP are the evaluation sets for generating verified code from specs. 'No fine-tuning' confirmed in the abstract. Authors include Aggarwal, Parno and Welleck; CMU affiliation is from my knowledge of them, not an affiliation line I read. Org confirmed from the arXiv HTML: all three authors at CMU (review 2026-11-03).
